mainTopic: Whose view do the rulings about a four-handbreadth beam follow, and do אביי and רבא in the סוכה case split along the lines of the רב and שמואל dispute over פי תקרה יורד וסותם?
overview: This amud finishes the chapter כל גגות and begins the chapter המוצא תפילין. First, the גמרא asks whose view two four-handbreadth beam rulings follow. It also checks whether the dispute between אביי and רבא about a סוכה on a portico is the same as the dispute between רב and שמואל. It concludes that the two disputes are not identical. Next, it explains that רבי יוסי meant to forbid carrying even on that same שבת. It then resolves an apparent contradiction in שמואל's rulings: he follows רבי יהודה when a breach opens into a כרמלית, but not when it opens into רשות הרבים. A new משנה follows: רבי יהודה permits carrying under an upper story or bridge, and making an עירוב for an alley open at both ends. רבה explains that the upper-story case rests on פי תקרה יורד וסותם, and רב אשי proves this from the word ועוד. After the הדרן, the new chapter opens with the case of someone who finds תפילין outside on שבת and brings them in by wearing them.

steps.title: Whose view do the two four-handbreadth beam rulings follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes two rulings that a four-handbreadth beam acts like a wall, one for a ruin and one for water, and asks whose view they follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: A beam four handbreadths wide permits carrying in a ruin. And רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: a beam four handbreadths wide permits carrying over water. Whose view are these?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two rulings that rely on a wide beam acting like a wall. It asks whose opinion they follow, since רב and שמואל argued about this idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both rulings only work if the edge of the beam counts as if it comes down and closes off the open side, which is the idea of פי תקרה יורד וסותם. The previous discussion showed that רב accepts this idea and שמואל does not, at least in some cases. So the גמרא needs to know which side these rulings belong to.

keyTerms.meaning: A beam laid across an opening
A ruin, a broken-down building with a breach
Permits (carrying)
Whose view is this?

phrases.english: A beam four handbreadths wide permits carrying in a ruin,
phrases.notes: The ruin is breached into a public domain, and the beam spans the breach.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: and that which Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
a beam four handbreadths wide permits carrying over water,
phrases.notes: The beam functions like a partition over the water.

phrases.english: whose view is this?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the earlier רב and שמואל dispute about פי תקרה יורד וסותם to two specific rulings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which side of the רב and שמואל dispute these two beam rulings follow.

steps.title: The answer depends on which version of the dispute you hold
steps.stepSummary: If רב and שמואל agree about gaps of up to ten, these rulings fit everyone. If they disagree even there, the rulings follow רב only.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the version that says they do not argue about a gap of ten, these rulings deal with a gap of ten and fit everyone's view. According to the version that says they do argue about ten, these rulings follow רב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers using the two versions of the רב and שמואל dispute that were stated earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In one version, even שמואל agrees that the beam closes off an opening up to ten אמות. In that version, the two rulings speak about such an opening, and everyone accepts them. In the other version, שמואל disagrees even there, so the rulings can only follow רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Version (of a teaching)
They disagree
Everyone agrees

steps.confusionAlert: The 'ten' here means an opening ten אמות wide. It does not mean ten handbreadths.

phrases.english: According to this version that you stated,
that with regard to ten they do not disagree:
it refers to an opening of ten, and it is everyone's view.
According to that version that you stated,
that they disagree even with regard to ten:
it is in accordance with Rav.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְהַךְ לִישָּׁנָא דְּאָמְרַתְּ בְּעֶשֶׂר לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of whose view the beam rulings follow.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In the first version, the rulings are about openings up to ten and fit everyone. In the second version, they follow רב alone.
steps.whatToRemember: Whose view the beam rulings follow depends on the version: either everyone's (for openings up to ten) or רב alone.

steps.title: Suggesting that אביי and רבא repeat the רב and שמואל dispute in the סוכה case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that אביי and רבא argue about the same point as רב and שמואל. It quotes their dispute about a portico with no doorposts used as a סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say that אביי and רבא disagree about the same point as רב and שמואל. For it was stated: if one put סכך on a portico that has doorposts, the סוכה is valid. If it has no doorposts, אביי says it is valid and רבא says it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new suggestion: maybe the later אמוראים, אביי and רבא, are really arguing the same dispute as רב and שמואל. Here it quotes their case, and the next steps explain and complete the suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אכסדרה is a roofed porch with no real walls. If it has doorposts, those give it the start of walls, so everyone agrees the סוכה is valid. The argument is only when it has no doorposts at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion)
Portico, a roofed porch without full walls
Doorposts or pillars that begin a wall
He put down סכך (the roofing of a סוכה)
Valid / invalid

phrases.english: Let us say that Abaye and Rava
disagree about the dispute of Rav and Shmuel,
as it was stated:
if one placed sukka-roofing on top of a portico
that has doorposts, it is valid;
if it has no doorposts,
Abaye said: it is valid,
and Rava said: it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the beam rulings to a proposed link between two separate disputes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the אביי and רבא dispute is the same as the רב and שמואל dispute.

steps.title: Explaining the reasoning of אביי and רבא
steps.stepSummary: אביי validates the סוכה because he holds פי תקרה יורד וסותם. רבא invalidates it because he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said it is valid, because he holds that the edge of the roof comes down and closes it in. רבא said it is invalid, because he does not hold that the edge of the roof comes down and closes it in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind each side, which sets up the comparison to רב and שמואל in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, the edge of the portico's roof creates virtual walls, so the סוכה has the walls it needs. For רבא, there are no virtual walls, so a portico without doorposts has no walls at all. This is exactly the point רב and שמואל argued about.

keyTerms.meaning: The edge of the roof is seen as coming down and sealing the side

phrases.english: Abaye said it is valid,
because he says the edge of the roof descends and seals.
And Rava said it is invalid,

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמַר פִּי תִקְרָה יוֹרֵד וְסוֹתֵם.
phrases.english: because he does not say the edge of the roof descends and seals.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר כְּשֵׁירָה, אָמַר פִּי תִקְרָה יוֹרֵד וְסוֹתֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the dispute just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute between אביי and רבא depends on whether one holds פי תקרה יורד וסותם.

steps.title: So is אביי following רב and רבא following שמואל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its suggestion: אביי matches רב, and רבא matches שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that אביי holds like רב, and רבא holds like שמואל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states its suggestion outright: the later dispute seems to line up with the earlier one. The following text will check whether this is really so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב accepted פי תקרה יורד וסותם, as אביי does, and שמואל rejected it, as רבא does. The word לימא hints that the גמרא will likely push back and show that the two disputes are not identical.

keyTerms.meaning: In accordance with רב
In accordance with שמואל

steps.confusionAlert: A 'לימא' suggestion is usually rejected later. Do not treat it as the final conclusion.

phrases.english: Let us say that Abaye holds like Rav,
and Rava holds like Shmuel?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא אַבָּיֵי כְּרַב, וְרָבָא כִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion of the suggestion, based on the reasoning explained in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether אביי and רבא simply repeat the positions of רב and שמואל.

steps.title: רבא can also agree with רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that אביי and רבא match רב and שמואל. Everyone agrees according to שמואל. They argue only about how far רב's view goes.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to שמואל, nobody argues: the סוכה is invalid. They argue only according to רב. אביי follows רב plainly. רבא says that רב only said the roof edge counts as a wall there, because those walls were made for the portico. But here, those walls were not made for a סוכה, so even רב would say no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion from step 5. אביי and רבא do not have to match רב and שמואל. Both of them can accept רב's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שמואל is right, even אביי would invalidate the סוכה. The real argument is about how far רב's rule reaches. רבא limits פי תקרה יורד וסותם to cases where the 'wall' serves the structure it was built for. The portico's roof edge was built for the portico, not for a סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: according to the view of
everyone agrees
he only said his rule up to this point (it is limited to this case)
made for, built for
partitions, walls

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as רבא arguing with רב. רבא accepts רב's rule. He just says it does not stretch to a סוכה, because these walls were not made for a סוכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches that a halachic 'virtual wall' can work for one purpose and fail for another, depending on what it was made for.

phrases.english: According to Shmuel
everyone agrees (the sukka is invalid).
Where they disagree is according to Rav:
Abaye holds like Rav.

phrases.aramaic: וְרָבָא — עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַב הָתָם,
phrases.english: And Rava says: Rav only said his rule there,
because those partitions were made for the portico.
But here,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָנֵי מְחִיצוֹת לָאו לְסוּכָּה עֲבִידִי — לָא.
phrases.english: where these partitions were not made for a sukka, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דִשְׁמוּאֵל כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison suggested in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that אביי matches רב and רבא matches שמואל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא can accept רב's rule and still invalidate the סוכה, because the portico's walls were not made for a סוכה.

steps.title: Did רבי יוסי mean to forbid or to permit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי's words in the משנה. It asks which way he meant them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי יוסי says, 'If they are permitted...' A question was asked: did רבי יוסי mean to forbid, or to permit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes רבי יוסי. It asks what his statement actually means, which sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said carrying is permitted on that שבת but forbidden in the future. רבי יוסי said the two times must be the same. That leaves it unclear whether he forbids both times or permits both times.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was asked before the scholars
to forbid
to permit
they are permitted

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: If they are permitted...
A question was asked before them:
Did Rabbi Yosei mean to forbid, or to permit?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לֶאֱסוֹר, אוֹ לְהַתִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by going back to the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יוסי forbids carrying even on that שבת, or permits it even in the future.

steps.title: רב ששת and רבי יוחנן: he meant to forbid
steps.stepSummary: Two אמוראים answer that רבי יוסי meant to forbid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: to forbid. And רבי יוחנן said the same: to forbid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the answer to the question. רב ששת and רבי יוחנן both say רבי יוסי meant to forbid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this reading, carrying is forbidden in the future, so רבי יוסי forbids it even on that same שבת. This is the opposite of רבי יהודה, who permits that שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: and likewise said

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: to forbid.
And likewise Rabbi Yochanan said: to forbid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: לֶאֱסוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי meant to forbid carrying even on that שבת.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the forbidding reading
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי saying clearly that carrying is forbidden on that שבת too.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא. רבי יוסי said: just as they are forbidden in the future, so they are forbidden on that שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the answer of רב ששת and רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי יוסי speaks openly. The future ban carries back to that same שבת. That settles the question in favor of 'to forbid.'

keyTerms.meaning: it was also taught this way (in a ברייתא)
in the future, after this שבת
just as... so too

phrases.english: It was also taught this way in a baraita:
Rabbi Yosei said:
Just as they are forbidden in the future,
so too they are forbidden on that Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer given in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that רבי יוסי meant to forbid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי יוסי says the future ban also applies on that שבת.

steps.title: The halachic ruling: רבי יוסי or רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר יוסף rules like רבי יוסי. שמואל rules like רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב חייא בר יוסף said the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, and שמואל said the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give opposite rulings on the dispute in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following רבי יוסי means carrying is forbidden even on that שבת. Following רבי יהודה means carrying is permitted on that שבת but forbidden afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: the practical law follows

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי forbids carrying even on that שבת, and a ברייתא confirms this. On the ruling, רב חייא בר יוסף follows רבי יוסי, while שמואל follows רבי יהודה, who permits that שבת.

phrases.english: It was stated:
Rav Chiyya bar Yosef said:
the halacha follows Rabbi Yosei,
and Shmuel said:
the halacha follows Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, רַב חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from what רבי יוסי meant to which view is the practical halacha.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חייא בר יוסף rules like רבי יוסי (forbidden even that שבת). שמואל rules like רבי יהודה (permitted that שבת).

steps.title: Did שמואל really say that? The גמרא quotes a משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא expresses surprise at שמואל's ruling and begins its challenge by quoting a משנה where רבי יהודה says an עירוב חצרות can be made for someone even without his knowledge.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did שמואל really say this? But we learned in a משנה that רבי יהודה said: When do we need the person to know about the עירוב? Only for עירובי תחומין. But for עירובי חצרות, we may make an עירוב for him whether he knows or not. This is because we may act for a person's benefit when he is not there, but we may not act against his interest when he is not there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised by שמואל's ruling from Step 10. It starts building a challenge by quoting a משנה of רבי יהודה, which sets up the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה alone is not yet the attack. It is the base text that שמואל's general rule about רבי יהודה (Step 12) is built on. The real tension only appears once רב יהודה explains how far that rule reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say...? An expression of surprise that opens a challenge
An עירוב that extends how far a person may walk on שבת
An עירוב that lets neighbors carry between their houses and a shared courtyard
We may act for someone's benefit even when he is not present
We may not act against someone's interest when he is not present

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה quoted here is not about fallen walls. It is brought only because it leads into שמואל's general statement about רבי יהודה in the next step.

phrases.english: And did Shmuel really say this?!
But didn't we learn in a mishna: Rabbi Yehuda said:
In what case is this said? With joinings of Shabbat boundaries.
phrases.notes: The rule being limited is that an עירוב needs the person's knowledge.

phrases.english: But with joinings of courtyards,

phrases.aramaic: מְעָרְבִין בֵּין לְדַעַת בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא לְדַעַת,
phrases.english: one may make an eiruv whether he knows or does not know,
because one may act for a person's benefit when he is not present,
but one may not act to his disadvantage when he is not present.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הָכִי?! וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling from Step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling in our case of a wall that fell on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: quotes the משנה that שמואל's general rule about רבי יהודה is attached to. The contradiction becomes clear in Steps 12 to 14.

steps.title: שמואל's general rule: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה in עירובין
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה in that משנה, and in every place he teaches in עירובין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה. And more than that, wherever רבי יהודה taught a law about עירובין, the הלכה follows him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues building its challenge. It brings שמואל's broad rule about רבי יהודה in עירובין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the key statement for the challenge. Next, the גמרא will show how far this rule reaches, and that limit is what creates the problem with our case.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but... (adds a wider statement)
Every place where he taught
The final law follows his view

steps.whyThisMatters: This general rule, that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה in עירובין, is an important guide for deciding the law in this whole מסכת.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
The halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda.
And not only that, but

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁשָּׁנָה רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּעֵירוּבִין —
phrases.english: every place where Rabbi Yehuda taught about eiruvin,
the halakha follows him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives שמואל's ruling on the משנה quoted in Step 11 and widens it into a general rule
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling in our fallen-wall case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Brings the general rule whose limits (Steps 13 and 14) will clash with שמואל's ruling in our case

steps.title: רב חנא asks: does this rule apply even to an alley that lost its beam or post?
steps.stepSummary: רב חנא בגדתאה asks רב יהודה whether שמואל's rule covers an alley whose קורה or לחי was removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנא from Baghdad said to רב יהודה: Did שמואל say this even about an alley whose קורה or לחיים were removed?
steps.whatsHappening: Someone asks how far שמואל's general rule goes. Does it also cover cases where the partitions of an alley were removed?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An alley's קורה (beam) and לחי (side post) work as its partitions. רב חנא wants to know whether 'everywhere in עירובין' also includes laws of partitions, where רבי יהודה is lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: An alleyway that courtyards open into
A beam placed across the entrance of an alley
Side posts at the entrance of an alley

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חָנָא בַּגְדָּתָאָה לְרַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: And Rav Ḥana of Baghdad said to Rav Yehuda:
Did Shmuel say this even
about an alleyway whose cross beam or side posts were removed?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חָנָא בַּגְדָּתָאָה לְרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the scope of the general rule from Step 12
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does שמואל's 'follow רבי יהודה in עירובין' include cases of removed partitions?

steps.title: רב יהודה: the rule is about עירובין, not partitions
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that שמואל's rule was said about עירובין, not about מחיצות. This completes the challenge against שמואל's ruling in our fallen-wall case.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I told you this about עירובין, not about partitions.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה limits שמואל's rule. It does not cover partitions. That answer finishes the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So in matters of partitions, שמואל does not automatically follow רבי יהודה. Our משנה, a courtyard wall that fell on שבת, is a partitions case. So how could שמואל rule like רבי יהודה there?

keyTerms.meaning: Partitions or walls that define a private area
I told you

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two subjects. 'עירובין' here means the laws of joining (making the עירוב itself). 'מחיצות' means the walls and partitions. שמואל's general rule covers only the first.

phrases.english: And he said to him: I told you this about eiruvin,
and not about partitions.
phrases.notes: The hidden question: our משנה is about a fallen wall, and that's exactly a partitions case.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּעֵירוּבִין אָמַרְתִּי לְךָ, וְלֹא בִּמְחִיצוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חנא's question, which sharpens the challenge against Step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל's rule applies only to laws of עירובין, not to laws of partitions. This implies he does not follow רבי יהודה in partition cases, which clashes with his ruling in our fallen-wall case.

steps.title: רב ענן: it depends on where the breach opens
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן reports that שמואל himself explained the difference. In one case the breach opens into a כרמלית, so we follow רבי יהודה. In the other it opens into רשות הרבים, so we do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן said: שמואל himself explained this to me. Here, the courtyard was breached into a כרמלית. There, it was breached into רשות הרבים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. שמואל's two statements are about different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the breach opens into a כרמלית, carrying there is only forbidden by the Rabbis. So שמואל can be lenient like רבי יהודה. When it opens into רשות הרבים, there is a risk of breaking a Torah prohibition. So שמואל does not follow רבי יהודה, and he is strict.

keyTerms.meaning: It was explained to me personally
Was breached (a wall broke open)
An in-between area where carrying is forbidden only by the Rabbis
Public domain, where carrying is forbidden by the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל is consistent. With a fallen wall, he follows רבי יהודה (lenient) when the breach opens into a כרמלית. He does not follow him (strict) when it opens into רשות הרבים, because a Torah prohibition is at stake.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a practical line for fallen-wall cases. The level of the prohibition at stake, Rabbinic or Torah, decides whether we are lenient.

phrases.english: Rav Anan said:
It was explained to me personally by Shmuel:
Here, it was breached into a karmelit,
phrases.notes: Here the הלכה follows רבי יהודה (lenient).

phrases.english: there, it was breached into a public domain.
phrases.notes: There the הלכה does not follow רבי יהודה (strict).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עָנָן: לְדִידִי מִיפָּרְשָׁא לִי מִינֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Steps 11 to 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting cases: the two statements apply to different situations
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל seemed to both follow and not follow רבי יהודה in partition cases
steps.terutzMaskana: He follows רבי יהודה when the breach opens into a כרמלית (Rabbinic level) and does not when it opens into רשות הרבים (Torah level)

steps.title: Carrying under an upper story or bridge
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה: רבי יהודה permits carrying beneath an upper story built over two houses, and beneath open bridges. The חכמים forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone builds an upper room resting on two houses, with a public path running underneath. The same applies to bridges that are open at both ends. רבי יהודה says you may carry underneath them on שבת. The חכמים forbid it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes a covered area with walls on two sides and openings on the other two sides, and records a מחלוקת about carrying there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture two houses facing each other across a path, with a room built on top that connects them. The space underneath has two walls (the houses) and a roof, but its front and back are open. רבי יהודה treats it as a private area. The חכמים do not.

keyTerms.meaning: An upper story; a room built on top
Bridges
Open straight through, from end to end
One may carry (move objects)

phrases.english: MISHNAH
One who builds an upper story
on top of two houses,
phrases.notes: The houses stand on opposite sides of a public path.

phrases.english: and likewise bridges that are open through
one may carry beneath them on Shabbat,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
And the Sages forbid.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַבּוֹנֶה עֲלִיָּיה עַל גַּבֵּי שְׁנֵי בָתִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous סוגיא about a fallen wall.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: one may carry under an upper story spanning two houses and under open bridges. חכמים: forbidden.

steps.title: Making an עירוב for an alley open at both ends
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה adds that one may make an עירוב for an alley open at both ends. The חכמים forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה also said: you can make an עירוב for an alley that is open at both ends. The חכמים forbid it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second, related ruling from רבי יהודה, again disputed by the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An alley open at both ends also has only two walls, its two sides. רבי יהודה is lenient here too, which fits his lenient view in the upper-story case.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; adding another ruling
One may make an עירוב
An alley

phrases.english: And furthermore Rabbi Yehuda said:
One may make an eruv for an alley that is open at both ends.
And the Sages forbid.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second leniency of רבי יהודה to the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה permits an עירוב for a מבוי מפולש; the חכמים forbid it.

steps.title: רבה explains רבי יהודה's reason: the roof edge closes the sides
steps.stepSummary: רבה says רבי יהודה's reason is not that two walls are enough מדאורייתא. It is that the edge of the roof is seen as coming down to close the open sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבה said: Do not think רבי יהודה's reason is that two walls make a private area by Torah law. Rather, he holds that the edge of the roof is treated as if it comes down and closes off the open sides.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins, and רבה explains why רבי יהודה permits carrying under the upper story. He rejects one possible reason and gives a different one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two reasons are possible. (1) Two walls are already enough to make a private area by Torah law. (2) The roof's edge acts like an imaginary wall hanging down to seal the open sides. רבה picks reason (2), so for him the roof is essential to רבי יהודה's leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: Two walls are enough by Torah law to make a private domain
The edge of a roof
Comes down and closes (treated as a wall)
Do not say (do not think)

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not saying two walls are useless. He is only saying that two walls are not the reason רבי יהודה permits carrying here. The reason is the roof.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because רבה ties רבי יהודה's view to the roof, any case where רבי יהודה is lenient without a roof becomes a problem for him. That is exactly what אביי will bring next.

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rabbah said:

phrases.aramaic: לָא תֵּימָא הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: Do not say that this is Rabbi Yehuda's reason:
because he holds
that two walls make a private domain by Torah law.
Rather, it is because he holds:
the edge of the roof comes down and closes off the sides.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי יהודה's ruling in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה's leniency is based on פי תקרה יורד וסותם, not on two walls being enough מדאורייתא.

steps.title: אביי objects: רבי יהודה is lenient even with no roof
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא in which רבי יהודה lets a person carry between two houses on opposite sides of רשות הרבים using only a לחי or קורה. There is no roof there, so the roof cannot be his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged רבה from a ברייתא. רבי יהודה said even more: a person has two houses on two sides of a public road. He sets up a side post here and a side post there, or a beam here and a beam there. Then he may carry and put things down in the middle. The חכמים said to him: you cannot turn a public road into a private area this way!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's explanation. He quotes a ברייתא where רבי יהודה is lenient in a case that has no roof at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the space between the two houses is open to the sky, so פי תקרה יורד וסותם cannot apply. רבי יהודה still permits carrying. That suggests his real reason is that two walls (the two houses) are enough מדאורייתא, which is the very reason רבה rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: Even more than this (an even bigger leniency)
Carries and places objects
In the middle

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא never says 'two walls are enough.' אביי infers it: with no roof, the only thing left that could make this a private area is the two houses acting as walls.

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Even more than this, Rabbi Yehuda said:
One who has two houses
on two sides of the public domain
makes a side post here and a side post there,
or a crossbeam here and a crossbeam there,
and he may carry and place objects in the middle.
They said to him:
One cannot make an eruv for a public domain in this way!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's explanation of רבי יהודה's reason.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that רבי יהודה relies on פי תקרה יורד וסותם and not on שתי מחיצות דאורייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא there is no roof, yet רבי יהודה permits carrying with only a לחי or קורה. So his leniency cannot depend on a roof edge. It must rest on two walls being enough מדאורייתא.

steps.title: רבה: The ברייתא proves it, the משנה does not
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers אביי. The ברייתא does show that רבי יהודה holds two walls are enough מדאורייתא. But the משנה about the upper story cannot prove that, because there the reason is the edge of the roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: From that ברייתא, yes, you can learn it. From this משנה, you cannot learn it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers אביי's challenge from the ברייתא. He agrees with part of it and pushes back on the rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה agrees that in the ברייתא there is no roof, so there רבי יהודה must hold that two walls are enough מדאורייתא. But רבי יהודה can hold both ideas. In the upper-story case of the משנה, רבה still says the reason is פי תקרה יורד וסותם, not the two walls.

keyTerms.meaning: From that one (the ברייתא אביי quoted)
From this one (our משנה)
Yes
There is nothing to learn from it

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not taking back his view. He is saying רבי יהודה holds BOTH ideas: two walls are enough מדאורייתא, AND the roof edge closes the sides. In the משנה's case, the roof edge is the reason.

phrases.english: He (Rabba) said to him (Abaye):
From that one (the baraita) — yes,
phrases.notes: There is no roof there, so the reason must be two walls.

phrases.english: from this one (the mishna) — there is nothing to learn from it.
phrases.notes: In the mishna there is a roof, so the roof edge can be the reason.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מֵהַהִיא — אִין, מֵהָא — לֵיכָּא לְמִשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's קשיא from Step 19 by limiting what each source proves.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Partial concession: two different sources, two different reasons
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the ברייתא shows רבי יהודה holds two walls are enough, that must also be his reason in the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה holds both ideas. In the משנה's upper-story case, the roof edge is the reason.

steps.title: רב אשי: The wording of the משנה supports רבה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the משנה's own wording supports רבה. It introduces the open-alley ruling with "ועוד" ("and furthermore").
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The משנה is also precise this way. It teaches: "And furthermore, רבי יהודה said: one may make an עירוב for an alley open at both ends, and the חכמים forbid it."
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings support for רבה from the exact wording of the משנה. This step sets up the proof that comes in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is "ועוד", which means "and furthermore." A משנה says "furthermore" when it adds something new, not when it repeats the same idea. רב אשי will now show why this word fits only רבה's explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Precise; the exact wording shows it
And furthermore; adds a new point
An alley open at both ends
One may make an עירוב

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The mishna is also precise (in this way),
since it teaches:
"And furthermore, Rabbi Yehuda said:
One may make an eiruv for an alley open at both ends,
and the Rabbis forbid it."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מַתְנִיתִין נָמֵי דַּיְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבה's position from Step 20 using the משנה quoted in Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's claim that in the upper-story case רבי יהודה's reason is פי תקרה יורד וסותם

steps.title: If the reason is the roof edge, "ועוד" makes sense
steps.stepSummary: Suppose the upper-story ruling rests on the roof edge closing the sides. Then the alley ruling rests on a new reason, two walls. So "ועוד" fits well.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say רבי יהודה's reason is that the edge of the roof comes down and closes the sides. That is why the משנה says "and furthermore."
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי shows that רבה's explanation fits the word "ועוד".
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבה, the first ruling (upper story) depends on the roof edge. The second ruling (open alley) has no roof, so it depends on a different idea: two walls are enough. Two different reasons explain why the משנה needs the word "furthermore."

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say
The edge of the roof is seen as coming down and closing the side
That is why; this explains

phrases.english: It works well if you say
that it is because he holds
that the edge of the roof comes down and closes —
that is why it teaches "and furthermore."
phrases.notes: The alley case adds a new reason: two walls.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא סָבַר פִּי תִקְרָה יוֹרֵד וְסוֹתֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First half of the בשלמא/אלא proof begun in Step 21.
steps.raayaSupportSource: "ועוד" fits when the two rulings rest on two different reasons

steps.title: If the reason is two walls, "ועוד" makes no sense
steps.stepSummary: Suppose the upper-story ruling also rests on two walls being enough. Then both rulings share the same reason, and "ועוד" would be pointless.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say the reason is that he holds two walls are enough מדאורייתא, then why does it say "and furthermore"?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי shows that the other explanation does not fit the word "ועוד".
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose both the upper story and the open alley worked only because two walls are enough. Then the second ruling would add nothing new, and "furthermore" would be out of place. So the upper-story ruling must rest on a different reason, the roof edge.

keyTerms.meaning: Two walls are enough by Torah law to make a private domain
What? Why? (used to challenge)

phrases.english: But if you say
that it is because he holds
that two walls are enough by Torah law —
why "and furthermore"?!
phrases.notes: If it's the same reason twice, nothing new is being added.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא סָבַר שְׁתֵּי מְחִיצוֹת דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the בשלמא/אלא proof. It shows the rival explanation fails.
steps.raayaObject: Rejecting the idea that the upper-story ruling rests on two walls
steps.raayaSupportSource: "ועוד" would add nothing if both rulings shared one reason

steps.title: Conclusion: רבה's explanation is proven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבה is right. In the upper-story case, רבי יהודה's reason is פי תקרה יורד וסותם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this that it is so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רב אשי's proof and closes the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds two separate ideas. The roof edge permits the upper story and the bridges. Two walls being enough מדאורייתא permits the open alley and the ברייתא case. The word "ועוד" marks the move from one idea to the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; it is proven

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה has two different reasons. Upper story and bridges: the roof edge closes the sides (פי תקרה יורד וסותם). Open alley and the ברייתא: two walls are enough מדאורייתא. The word "ועוד" in the משנה shows they are different reasons.

phrases.english: Learn from this (that it is so).

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רב אשי's proof from Steps 21-23.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In the משנה's upper-story case, רבי יהודה's reason is פי תקרה יורד וסותם. His open-alley ruling rests on two walls being enough מדאורייתא.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter כל גגות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes the ninth chapter, כל גגות, with the traditional הדרן formula.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'כל גגות'.
steps.whatsHappening: The chapter about roofs, courtyards and alleys (כל גגות) is finished. The text marks its end with the הדרן line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 settled the last discussion: in the upper-story case, רבי יהודה's reason is פי תקרה יורד וסותם. With that, the chapter's topics are complete. הדרן is a farewell and a promise to come back and learn the chapter again.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We will return to you.' The formula said when a chapter is finished.
'All roofs.' The opening words and name of the chapter being closed.

steps.whatToRemember: The roofs-and-alleys chapter ends here. Everything after this line belongs to a new chapter with a new topic.

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'All roofs'
phrases.notes: This is what we say at the end of a chapter, which is named by its first words, כל גגות.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַדְרָן עֲלָךְ כׇּל גַּגּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the chapter whose final discussion ended in step 24.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter כל גגות is complete.

steps.title: Rescuing found תפילין by wearing them
steps.stepSummary: The new chapter's משנה opens. One who finds תפילין outside on שבת brings them in pair by pair. רבן גמליאל says two pairs at a time.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who finds תפילין brings them in pair by pair. רבן גמליאל says: two by two.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a new case. Someone finds תפילין lying outside on שבת and wants to save them, so the משנה tells him how to bring them in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you may not carry outside on שבת. But wearing תפילין is wearing clothing, not carrying. So he puts on one set, a head and an arm תפילין, walks home, takes it off, and returns for the next. רבן גמליאל adds that he may wear two sets at once, since there is room for two.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה.' It marks the start of the משנה text.
'One who finds תפילין.' The opening words and name of the new chapter.
'He brings them in' to a safe, private place.
'Pair by pair.' One set (head and arm) at a time, worn the normal way.
'Two by two.' Two pairs worn at the same time.

steps.confusionAlert: He does not carry the תפילין in his hands. He wears them, and that is why it is allowed. 'Pair' means a set of head and arm תפילין, not two loose boxes.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic rule of the whole new chapter. Wearing something the normal way counts as wearing, not carrying, so it is permitted on שבת.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who finds phylacteries
phrases.notes: Found outside on שבת, where they could be lost or ruined.

phrases.english: brings them in pair by pair.
phrases.notes: He wears one set at a time, the normal way.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel says:
Two by two.
phrases.notes: He may wear two sets at once.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמּוֹצֵא תְּפִילִּין מַכְנִיסָן זוּג זוּג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new chapter right after the הדרן that closed the previous one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Found תפילין may be brought in on שבת by wearing them. The תנא קמא allows one pair at a time; רבן גמליאל allows two pairs at a time.

steps.title: Only old תפילין, not new ones
steps.stepSummary: The משנה limits the rule. It applies only to old, used תפילין. With new ones the finder is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: When was this said? With old ones. But with new ones, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה narrows the rule it just gave. It says exactly which תפילין you may rescue by wearing them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Old תפילין have clearly been used, so we know they are real תפילין and wearing them counts as normal wearing. New ones might be only amulets shaped like תפילין. Since we are not sure, he does not have to bring them in.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When was this said?' A phrase that limits the ruling just given.
'Old ones.' תפילין that have already been worn.
'New ones.' Unused, so they may not be real תפילין.
'Exempt.' Here: he does not have to bring them in.

phrases.english: In what case is this statement said?
With regard to old ones,
but with regard to new ones, he is exempt.
phrases.notes: They may only be amulets in the shape of תפילין.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים בִּישָׁנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the permission of step 26 to old תפילין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The permission to bring found תפילין in by wearing them applies to old תפילין. With new ones he is פטור.

steps.title: Bundles: guard them until nightfall
steps.stepSummary: If the תפילין are tied in bundles or wrapped piles, he cannot wear them. So he stays with them until dark and then brings them home.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he found them tied in bundles or wrapped piles, he waits with them until dark and then brings them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a case where the wearing method will not work. It tells the finder what to do instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When many תפילין are tied or wrapped together, he cannot wear them one pair at a time. Carrying them would be a real איסור. So he guards them where they are, and after שבת ends he may carry them home.

keyTerms.meaning: Tied bundles.
Wrapped piles, rolled up together.
'Waits over them until dark.' He stays and guards them until שבת ends.
'And brings them,' meaning after שבת.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives three rules. Wear found תפילין home (one pair, or two according to רבן גמליאל). This applies only to old תפילין. If they are bundled and cannot be worn, guard them until nightfall.

phrases.english: If he found them in tied bundles or wrapped piles,
phrases.notes: So they cannot be worn pair by pair.

phrases.english: he waits over them until dark
phrases.notes: He guards them until שבת is over.

phrases.english: and brings them in.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְצָאָן צְבָתִים אוֹ כְרִיכוֹת מַחְשִׁיךְ עֲלֵיהֶן וּמְבִיאָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a case where the wearing method of step 26 cannot be used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bundled תפילין that cannot be worn are guarded until nightfall and then brought in.
